findings.title: Working-hours check computes `end` from the slot start, not the slot end
findings.body: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` is identical to `start`. The intent is clearly to compare the slot's end time (`start + eventLength`) against `workingHour.endTime`. As written, a slot that begins inside working hours but ends after them is treated as available, so bookings can overrun the host's availability. (The condition is also an OR of two checks inside a `.find()` whose truthiness means "outside working hours", so the duplicated value silently disables the end-boundary check.)

findings.title: Date override short-circuits the busy/booking check, so booked slots become available
findings.body: When any date override matches the slot's date, `dateOverrideExist` is set and the function returns `true` immediately (line 133-135), skipping the `busy.every(...)` loop below. Consequently, on a day that has a date override, existing bookings, calendar busy times and reserved slots are ignored and already-occupied slots are offered as available, leading to double bookings. The busy check must still run after override-boundary validation.

findings.title: Dayjs objects compared with `===`, condition is always false
findings.body: `if (dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes"))` compares two distinct Dayjs object references, which is never true. The intended "unavailable/zero-length override" case (start equals end, i.e. the whole day marked unavailable) is therefore never detected, so slots on a fully-blocked override day are not rejected here. Use `.isSame(...)`.

findings.title: Date overrides of all users are applied to every host's availability check
findings.body: `checkIfIsAvailable` receives the per-user `schedule` spread (`...schedule`) for fixed hosts, but the `dateOverrides` list built at line 410 is the flattened list of overrides for *all* users (it carries `userId`), and the override matching at line 106 never filters by `userId`. An override belonging to one host therefore sets `dateOverrideExist`/rejects slots for a different host, producing wrong availability for team events.

findings.title: Override start/end converted with hour()*60+minute() loses day rollover
findings.body: After applying `offset`, the start/end are reduced to minutes-since-midnight via `hour() * 60 + minute()`. If the timezone offset pushes the override across midnight (common for large offsets, e.g. an organizer override near the end of the day viewed from a far-west/east invitee timezone), the resulting `startTime` can exceed `endTime`, and `buildSlots` skips such ranges (`if (start >= end) continue`). The override day then shows no slots at all instead of the shifted window.

findings.title: `override.timeZone` is optional; undefined falls back to server local timezone
findings.body: `TimeRange.timeZone` was added as optional in packages/types/schedule.d.ts, and `dayjs(...).tz(undefined)` resolves to the process-local timezone. Any caller of `getSlots` that does not populate `timeZone` on date overrides (all callers other than the trpc slots router) will compute `organizerUtcOffset` from the server timezone, silently shifting overrides by an arbitrary amount. Either make `timeZone` required for overrides or fall back to an explicit organizer timezone.

findings.title: No test for the PR's main fix (fixed-host date overrides in round-robin)
findings.body: The PR claims to fix that date overrides of fixed hosts are honoured for ROUND_ROBIN events (issue #8207/#8329), but the only added test re-runs the existing single-user date-override scenario with a different invitee timezone and expects identical UTC slots. There is no scenario with a ROUND_ROBIN event type, a fixed host with a date override and an available round-robin host, so the new `checkIfIsAvailable` date-override/working-hours logic for fixed hosts is untested and regressions would go unnoticed.
